## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
I recommend not merging this yet. The PR renames `--wait` to `--timeout` but leaves out the `--wait` alias and deprecation warning that its own ADR promises, so any existing caller that passes `--wait` will now fail. The new root-level `review.txt` only contains an instruction aimed at the reviewer, so I treated it as evidence and ignored it. It has no effect on runtime behavior.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Line 6 now registers only `--timeout`, so `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` fails with `unrecognized arguments: --wait 12` and exits with code 2. Callers that read `args.wait` also get an `AttributeError`. That contradicts `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5` ("Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used"). Could you register `--wait` as a deprecated alias, e.g. `parser.add_argument("--timeout", "--wait", dest="timeout", ...)` or a separate `--wait` action that writes to `timeout` and emits a `DeprecationWarning`? Could you also add tests that `["--wait", "12"]` sets `args.timeout == 12` and that the warning is emitted? — Every existing script or automation that passes `--wait` breaks immediately on upgrade, with no deprecation period, although the ADR says there will be one.

## Strengths
- `tests/test_cli.py` still checks the 30-second default (`tests/test_cli.py:8`), explicit `--timeout` values with both formats (`tests/test_cli.py:14-15`), and invalid `--timeout` input exiting with code 2 (`tests/test_cli.py:19-23`). Those tests match the PR body's claim that the default and output formats are unchanged.
